title: 2017 Baulkham Hills Legal Studies Trial
notes: Question 2 has no accurate listed answer (education and training in prison is rehabilitation); D is a closest-choice guess and must be reviewed. The PDF has no answer key. Question 19 alternatives have duplicated “a)” labels and are mapped in printed order.

questions.stem: Mark has been charged with an indictable offence. He pleads guilty at the committal hearing. Which of the following is a mitigating factor in his sentencing?
questions.answerNote: Remorse is mitigating; Weapon use, a child victim and abuse of position are aggravating.

questions.stem: The government expands education and skills training in prison. What is this is an example of?
questions.answerNote: Prison education and training is rehabilitation, which is absent from the choices; D is the closest remaining option but does not accurately describe the measure.

questions.stem: How are Human Rights best protected in Australia?

options.D: Statute law and the International Court of Justice

questions.answerNote: Domestic common law and legislation provide the main directly enforceable rights protections in Australia.

questions.stem: Belinda has been charged with a criminal offence and applies for bail in court which is refused. Why could the court have refused bail?

options.B: Belinda presents a risk to the community
options.C: Belinda has been charged with a serious crime

questions.answerNote: Flight risk, danger to the community and offence seriousness can each inform a bail refusal.

questions.stem: How can a human right that is protected in the Constitution be changed?
questions.answerNote: A referendum is required to change the Constitution.

questions.stem: In what criminal matter does the presumption of innocence NOT apply?

options.C: When the defendant is granted bail

questions.answerNote: Strict liability removes the usual requirement to prove mens rea.

questions.stem: A judge discovers during a criminal trial that she knows the defendant. What action should the judge take?

options.C: Disqualify herself from hearing the matter
options.D: Direct the jury to disregard this knowledge

questions.answerNote: A judge who may be conflicted should recuse herself to preserve impartiality.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a transnational crime?

options.A: Being charged with a criminal offence overseas

questions.answerNote: Drug trafficking is a standard example of transnational crime.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the role of The International Declaration of Human Rights?

options.C: A tool of the International Court of Justice
options.D: A general statement of basic human rights

questions.answerNote: The UDHR is a declaration of principles, not an enforceable treaty.

questions.stem: What is the role of a judge in a summary trial for an indictable offence?

options.A: To decide upon the facts, the verdict and the sentence

questions.answerNote: In a summary hearing the judicial officer finds facts and determines verdict and sentence.

questions.stem: What is removed when Parliament legislates a non parole period for an offence?

options.A: The right to appeal the sentence
options.C: The right to appeal the verdict
options.D: The right to apply for bail

questions.answerNote: A legislated non-parole period constrains judicial sentencing discretion.

questions.stem: Kerrie commits an offence when she is 12 years old. What must the prosecution prove?

options.A: That she had the necessary mens rea
options.B: That doli incapax does not apply
options.C: That she committed the crime on the balance of probabilities
options.D: That she was not insane at the time of the offence

questions.answerNote: The prosecution must rebut doli incapax for a 12-year-old by showing knowledge of serious wrongness.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a sentencing option reflecting the incapacitation purpose of punishment?
questions.answerNote: Life imprisonment incapacitates by preventing the offender from returning to the community.

questions.stem: Laezwen is a nation in the South Pacific Ocean which refuses to recognise basic human rights in its legal system. What power gives this nation the ability to ignore these rights?
questions.answerNote: State sovereignty includes authority over a state’s internal affairs.

questions.stem: For what crimes can the Australian Federal Police arrest offenders?
questions.answerNote: Terrorism and drug importation are Commonwealth offences investigated by the AFP.

questions.stem: Which court has the jurisdiction to deal with crimes against humanity?
questions.answerNote: The ICC prosecutes individuals for crimes against humanity.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors prompted changes to the Bail Act 2013?
questions.answerNote: Public and political pressure has been a significant driver of bail law changes.

questions.stem: Defendants who are convicted of crimes in the District court can appeal to the Supreme Court challenging the Courts decision. What can they challenge?

options.D: The Constitutional validity of the law

questions.answerNote: An appeal may challenge the conviction, the sentence, or both.

questions.stem: What type of offence is larceny?
questions.answerNote: Larceny is a property offence classified as economic; The printed choice labels are duplicated and mapped in order.

questions.stem: Who is entitled to Legal Aid ?

options.A: Those charged with an indictable offence
options.B: Those charged with a summary offence

questions.answerNote: Indictable matters are the best fit among these options, although actual Legal Aid eligibility also depends on means and merits.
